To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel approach for active learning on graph neural networks, called information gain propagation, which is able to select informative nodes to be labelled with relaxed queries, i.e., a human expert is only required to judge the correctness of the predictions, instead of the exact labels.

we introduce the first GNN-based active learning method with relaxed queries and a new information gain propagation criterion, and that it outperforms the current state of the art in terms of accuracy and labeling cost.
we propose a new way to graph active learning by introducing soft labels and relaxing the query.

the following questions: i) what is the impact of the number of labeled nodes on the accuracy of the GNN-based classification task? ii) how can we efficiently select the most valuable nodes for GNN-based classification? and iii) how can we design a new AL method for GNNs with relaxed queries and the soft label approach?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper proposes a novel approach for active learning with soft labels on graph neural networks, which significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both accuracy and labeling costs.
our method significantly improves the labeling efficiency and achieves the state-of-the art performance on the public datasets.
our method is able to improve the labeling accuracy while reducing the labeling cost, compared to the baselines, and that the improvement is more significant when the labeling cost is higher.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we introduce the idea of soft labels in the context of GNN-based Active learning.
we propose a new way of doing active learning with graph data, which can be seen as an alternative to the existing approaches.
we propose a novel active learning method for graph neural networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we propose a new way to do active learning on GNNs, which is to propagate the information gain of selected nodes to unlabeled ones.
the information gain propagation is a more appropriate criterion for AL than the existing node classification-based criteria.
the soft-label approach can greatly reduce the cost of labeling and thus make the AL more practical.
